title: What the venture literature says about team against business
purpose: Shown beside a partner's own order as a point of comparison, never as a default and never as weights. Ordinal only: the sources rank kinds of evidence; they give no percentages.
criteria_note: Mapped onto the venture-screening tree's top level: team = Team; business = Problem and solution (product), Market. Traction is left out because neither source names it.

variants.name: Stated by VCs
variants.summary: VCs rate the team as more important than the business, and attribute more of a company's success or failure to the team.

citations.authors: Gompers, P., Gornall, W., Kaplan, S. N. and Strebulaev, I. A.
citations.title: How do venture capitalists make decisions?
citations.where: Journal of Financial Economics (2020); NBER Working Paper 22587 (2016)

variants.name: Outcome-predictive
variants.summary: Team assessments best explain early funding of at least $1M, but not larger rounds or success; market and product explain later rounds (above $10M, $25M and $50M) and longer-term outcomes. The authors suggest VCs may overweight team.

citations.authors: Jang, Y. and Kaplan, S. N.
